rationale: Iteration 8 is the best raced design (690.5). It finishes the oval 20/20 (2.41 s) and the s-bend 20/20 (2.79 s), with slalom at 0/20 (progress 0.52, 17 off-track, 3 timeouts). Every later change either regressed or gave no clear gain. Iteration 7 (kp 6.0 with a wider sensor spread) collapsed the oval and s-bend to 0 finishes. Iteration 9 (wheel_track 0.09) scored 676, and iteration 10 (kd 2.2) scored 685, both below iteration 8. With no further iteration after this one, a single untested change to the final design carries real risk on the unseen track, so I am resubmitting the iteration-8 geometry and controller unchanged. Its evidence is 60 trials, with 40 of 40 finishes on the two bend-heavy tracks it can complete. The main weakness is the slalom, where failures are off-track exits at sharp direction changes (max_error about 0.06 m). If it were possible to test further, the next levers would be a lower base_speed on tight sections or a modest kd change, but I am not changing them here. Expected result: the same score as iteration 8, about 690 on the development tracks. Hypotheses: H1, the design is stable across seeds, shown by oval and s-bend completion holding at 100%. H2, the slalom remains the limit, shown by progress staying near 0.5. Measurements requested: completion, progress and completion_time for speed versus finishing, max_error and line_loss_events for stability, steering_oscillation for damping, and noise_robustness for margin on the unseen track.
